prompts.instructions: Your athlete just finished a set. Give three beats in 2-3 short sentences, in whatever order feels natural: one takeaway about the set, ONE specific thing to do next set if a fault kept repeating, and one specific thing that went well — a CUE OUTCOME where the fix held is the best one. Plain qualitative words: whole numbers only where they help (a rep number, a cm adjustment, a score change), never decimals, degrees or seconds. Open differently than you did after the last set. No humor in this reply — keep it straight, supportive, and forward-looking. Here is the data: Set 1 of 2 just finished: 2 of 4 reps clean. Next up is set 2 of 2. Load: 60 kg. Depth was very consistent from rep to rep. Rep speed: the last reps slowed down a lot — close to their limit. Faults: knees caving in on 1 of 4 reps; hips sliding to one side on 1 of 4 reps (approximate); heels lifting on 1 of 4 reps. Faults marked approximate are hard to judge from this camera setup — if you mention one, say it looked like it, never state it as fact. This set's focus was knees caving in. CUE OUTCOME: after your cue on knees caving in at rep 1, it was gone on reps 2 to 4 — name that improvement. Best rep: rep 2, their deepest clean rep. Roughest rep: rep 4 — hips sliding to one side, heels lifting. ATHLETE STATE: rep speed says they're near their limit — keep it calm and brief, lead with what went right, no humor.
prompts.last_set_note: Set 1: 2 of 4 reps clean; load 60 kg; focus knees caving in; cue 'Left knee out' at rep 1, gone after.

Last set — CUE OUTCOME: after your cue on knees caving in at rep 1, it still showed on 1 of the 3 reps after. Give honest feedback in 2-3 short sentences, in whatever order feels natural: how the sets went, one takeaway for next session, and one specific thing that went well. Plain qualitative words: whole numbers only where they help (a rep number, a score change), never decimals, degrees or seconds. No humor in this reply — keep it straight, supportive, and forward-looking. End warm and steady — they just finished.
